titleEn: Rear-End Collision at 32 Weeks Pregnant - Abdominal Pain and Spinal Precautions

patient.name: Hannah Lee
patient.affectEn: alert and anxious, 32 weeks pregnant; sitting on the curb beside a bystander with one hand on her lower abdomen; keeps turning her head toward the traffic and toward you until she is told to stay still; worried about the baby
patient.speechEn: full sentences, a little quick and tense; cooperative; answers what she is asked and does not volunteer extra details; mentions the baby moving less only when asked how she is or what is wrong

scene.settingEn: Granville Avenue at Garden City Road in Richmond at about 0848 hrs. Dry morning, 12 °C, light traffic held back by police. The fire engine is parked beside the crash with its lights on, and fire rescue says both vehicles are chocked and stable. The patient's sedan was hit from behind by a pickup truck at an estimated 60 km/h while stopped at a red light: the trunk is crushed, the rear seat area is pushed forward about 0.6 m into the passenger compartment, and the driver's airbag did not deploy. The pickup driver stands with a police officer and says he is uninjured. Two vehicles, one patient, sitting on the curb beside a bystander. Hospital is 9 minutes away.
hazardsEn: traffic on Granville Avenue - light, held back by police
two damaged vehicles - chocked and stable per fire rescue, fire engine parked beside the crash with its lights on

bystanders.who: bystander sitting beside her on the curb
bystanders.knowsEn: Saw the pickup hit the sedan from behind while the sedan was stopped at the red light. The driver climbed out of her car on her own and sat down on the curb, holding her lower belly and turning her head. Knows nothing about her medical history.

bystanders.who: pickup truck driver (standing with a police officer)
bystanders.knowsEn: Says he is uninjured. The police officer estimates the impact speed at about 60 km/h.
Both vehicles are chocked and stable. They will help with the lift onto the spinal device, the stretcher and egress when the candidate directs them, and act only on that direction.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: spinal immobilization device with body straps
oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
PCP only: IV start kit with tubing and normal saline

dispatchEn: 0848 hrs. Code 3 to Granville Avenue at Garden City Road in Richmond. Two-vehicle collision: a woman who is 32 weeks pregnant was rear-ended while stopped at a red light and complains of abdominal pain. Fire rescue and police are on scene. Hospital is 9 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: fire rescue reports both vehicles are stable and the driver has climbed out of her car and is sitting on the curb with a bystander; the other driver says he is uninjured.
arrivalEn: You pull up beside the fire engine, which is parked next to the crash with its lights on. Police have the light traffic held back. It is a dry morning, 12 degrees. Fire rescue tells you both vehicles are chocked and stable. A sedan that was stopped at the red light has been hit from behind by a pickup truck at an estimated 60 kilometres an hour: the sedan's trunk is crushed, the rear seat area is pushed forward about 0.6 metres into the passenger compartment, and the driver's airbag did not deploy. The pickup driver stands with a police officer and says he is uninjured. Two vehicles, one patient. Your patient is sitting on the curb beside a bystander.
firstLookEn: A visibly pregnant woman sitting on the curb beside a bystander, awake and alert, one hand on her lower abdomen. She keeps turning her head to look at you and at the traffic.

primary.locEn: Alert (AVPU = A). She answers appropriately and speaks in full sentences (GCS 15).
primary.airwayEn: Open and clear. She speaks in full sentences, no abnormal sounds.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 22, regular, no distress. Faint seat-belt redness runs diagonally across the chest, non-tender, with equal air entry.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 110, strong and regular. No major external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Rapid body survey: midline neck tenderness over the lower cervical spine; faint seat-belt redness across the chest, non-tender; a bruise across the lower abdomen above the pubic bone; gravid abdomen tender over the uterus with contractions about every 6 minutes; pelvis stable; a small amount of bright red blood on her underwear and pad, no clots; no head or face injury and no limb injuries. Skin is pale, warm, slightly moist (skin is given automatically with the RBS). SpO2 98% on room air if checked. (Examiner note, never volunteer: a high-risk crash with 0.6 m of intrusion, midline neck tenderness and a painful distracting abdominal injury mean NEXUS cannot clear her neck, so spinal motion restriction is indicated; climbing out of the car and walking to the curb does not clear her spine.)

history.ccEn: My stomach hurts and my neck hurts, and the baby isn't moving as much.

opqrst.oEn: It started right when the pickup hit me.
opqrst.pEn: Nothing I've tried makes either one better, and I haven't noticed anything that makes them worse.
opqrst.qEn: The belly pain is constant, with a cramping on top of it that comes and goes. The neck pain is at the back of my neck.
opqrst.rEn: The belly pain stays low in my belly. The neck pain is at the back of my neck, and I have a low back ache. No numbness or tingling in my arms or legs.
opqrst.sEn: My belly is about a 7 out of 10 and my neck is about a 4 out of 10.
opqrst.tEn: The belly pain has been constant since the crash, and the cramping comes and goes about every six minutes. The neck pain started then too.

history.painScoreEn: My belly is a 7 out of 10 and my neck is a 4 out of 10. (Only if asked again after BOTH Entonox and acetaminophen have been given: my belly is a 4 out of 10 and my neck is a 3 out of 10. If asked again before both have been given: still the same, a 7 and a 4.)

sample.sEn: My belly hurts with cramping that comes and goes about every six minutes, my neck hurts at the back, and I have a low back ache. I noticed a small amount of bright red bleeding down there about five minutes ago. No fluid is leaking, and the baby has been moving less than usual since the crash.
sample.aEn: No allergies that I know of.
sample.mEn: Just my prenatal vitamins. I haven't taken Tylenol, ibuprofen or anything else for pain today.
sample.pEn: I'm healthy. This is my second pregnancy and I'm 32 weeks along. I had one earlier birth, a vaginal delivery with no problems. This pregnancy has been uncomplicated; my last prenatal visit was two weeks ago and I'm due in about 8 weeks. No high blood pressure, no diabetes and no liver problems.
sample.lEn: Toast and tea at seven thirty this morning.
sample.eEn: I was stopped at the red light and saw the pickup in my mirror, and a second later it hit me from behind. I was driving, with my lap and shoulder belt on and my hands on the wheel. My head snapped back and then forward. I didn't black out and the airbag didn't go off. It was just the two vehicles, and the police think the pickup was going about 60 kilometres an hour. Afterwards I climbed out and walked to the curb.

fe.generalEn: I've been healthy, and my pregnancy has been uncomplicated.
fe.cnsEn: My neck hurts. No headache, and no numbness or tingling anywhere.
fe.cardiovascularEn: My heart is racing. No chest pain.
fe.giGuEn: Cramping low in my belly, but no nausea or vomiting. A small amount of bleeding down there, no fluid leaking, the baby is moving less than usual since the crash, and no urinary symptoms.
fe.integumentaryEn: I have bruises from the seat belt.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: My neck hurts and my lower back aches. No pain in my arms or legs.
fe.eentEn: No changes in my vision and no ringing in my ears.

findings.headNeckEn: Midline tenderness over the lower cervical spine, no step-off. No head or face injury. Any collar the candidate has applied is in place.
findings.chestLungsEn: Faint seat-belt redness running diagonally across the chest, non-tender. Clear, with equal air entry at all 6 sites.
findings.abdomenEn: Gravid abdomen, fundus between the umbilicus and the xiphoid. A bruise across the lower abdomen above the pubic bone. Tender over the uterus, firm during a contraction and soft between contractions (contractions about every 6 minutes). Not distended by bowel gas. A small amount of bright red blood on the pad, no fluid leaking. Pelvis stable, no tenderness. If re-examined after the second set of vitals: contractions continue about every 6 minutes and there is one more small stain on the pad.
findings.backEn: Mild low back ache, no step or deformity felt at the lift.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Circulation, sensation and movement intact in both legs. No injury.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Circulation, sensation and movement intact in both arms. No injury.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: about 6 min after set 1, en route: on the spinal device with oxygen, Entonox and acetaminophen given (or at 15 minutes); SBP drifting down and pulse up but still above 90, so no bolus

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: She keeps turning her head to look at the traffic and at you.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan collar and spinal device, oxygen, trauma pads, Entonox and oral acetaminophen, early transport
triggers: bring the collar and spinal device

expected.actionEn: Recognize a pregnant trauma patient with abdominal pain after a rear-end crash as a likely RTC and plan to ask about gestation, bleeding, contractions and fetal movement
Anticipate traffic and vehicle hazards; plan PPE incl eye protection
Assign crew roles before arrival: one member takes manual head stabilization on first contact, one handles scene, equipment and fire rescue
triggers: you hold the c-spine when we arrive
you take her head on first contact

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (traffic held by police, vehicles stable per fire rescue), environment, MOI (rear-end collision at about 60 km/h with 0.6 m rear intrusion), number of patients (1)
Don gloves and eye protection
First look: alert pregnant woman on the curb holding her lower abdomen and turning her head
Size up the vehicle damage (crushed trunk, rear seat area pushed in, no airbag deployment) to judge the severity of the mechanism
Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert
triggers: can you tell me your name
do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: At first contact tell her to keep her head still and manually stabilize the head and neck; spinal motion restriction is indicated (high-risk crash with intrusion, midline neck tenderness, painful distracting injury) - walking out of the car does not clear the spine (p.25, p.11)
Assess airway: clear, speaking in full sentences
triggers: she's talking so the airway is clear

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing with the chest exposed: rate, effort, chest wall (seat-belt redness), air entry both sides
Assess circulation: fast, strong radial pulse; look for external bleeding

Rapid body survey, exposing and examining with spinal precautions kept up: neck tenderness, chest, lower-abdominal seat-belt bruise, uterine tenderness and contractions, pelvis, vaginal bleeding, limbs
Note skin: pale, warm, slightly moist
Oxygen (indicated for trauma, p.11), titrated to keep SpO2 at or above 94% (p.50)
triggers: keep her sats at 94 or above

expected.actionEn: Position supine on the spinal device with one coordinated move (p.54 supine to support BP; p.32 limit movement), position of comfort as far as the device allows
triggers: lay her flat on the device

expected.actionEn: Categorize as RTC citing the p.7 mechanism criterion (high-risk crash, intrusion more than 0.5 m at any site) - not SBP under 90
Packaged and ready to load within 15 minutes, secondary survey en route
Direct fire rescue and the partner (lift onto the spinal device, stretcher, egress) and keep to one coordinated move
Keep her calm and informed: explain why she must stay still, stay with her, tell her the baby will be checked at hospital
triggers: the baby will be checked at hospital
we are taking care of you

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaints: lower abdominal pain and neck pain after a rear-end collision at 32 weeks pregnant
HxC/C with the critical MVC questions (p.12: impact speed, restraint, intrusion, airbags, LOC, vehicles) and the pregnancy questions: contractions, vaginal bleeding, fluid leaking, fetal movement
triggers: were you wearing a seat belt

expected.actionEn: Pain scores for the abdomen and the neck
PMHx incl obstetric history (second pregnancy, one earlier uncomplicated birth, no hypertension or diabetes)
Medications, and specifically whether acetaminophen or ibuprofen was already taken today (needed before analgesia)
Allergies
LOI
GCS with components
BP by auscultation - SBP 102 is above 90 so the p.54 number is not met, but note it with the pulse of 110: shock is anticipated in a pregnant patient with abdominal trauma and bleeding
Pulse rate/strength/rhythm
Respirations rate/depth/character
Skin hands-on: temperature, colour, condition
Pupils
SpO2 with calibration
FE - General health
triggers: how have you been feeling lately

expected.actionEn: FE - CNS (numbness or tingling with the neck pain)
FE - Respiratory
FE - Cardiovascular
FE - GI/GU (cramping, vaginal bleeding, fluid leaking, fetal movement - pertinent)
FE - Integumentary (seat-belt bruises)
FE - Musculoskeletal (neck and back)
triggers: pain in your arms or legs

expected.actionEn: FE - Endocrine
FE - EENT
Head/neck exam with the collar in place: midline tenderness, step-off, head and face injuries
triggers: look at the head and face

expected.actionEn: Chest exam with 6-site auscultation, bilateral comparison (rules out a pneumothorax before Entonox)
triggers: compare both sides of the chest

expected.actionEn: Abdomen and pelvis exam: gravid uterus, seat-belt bruise, uterine tenderness and tone with contractions, blood on the pad, pelvic stability
Back exam at the lift: low back ache, step or deformity
triggers: run my hand down the back
check the back at the lift

expected.actionEn: Lower extremities: CSM
Upper extremities: CSM

Spinal management per p.25: manual stabilization, hard collar, spinal immobilization device, foam rollers/blocks, body secured as appropriate, head not taped, one coordinated move; recheck CSM afterwards
triggers: secure her body to the device

expected.actionEn: Control the external (vaginal) bleeding with a pad, protect against heat loss, and check the pad at every reassessment (p.32, p.54)
Apply the Hypovolemia interventions on the anticipated-shock basis (p.54 note 2) and say so: SBP 102 is above 90, but the mechanism, abdominal injury, bleeding and pulse 110 make shock likely
Before any analgesic: baseline vitals done and each drug's contraindications ruled out (p.58, p.65, p.68); withhold ibuprofen - pregnancy is a listed contraindication in every trimester (p.68)
Acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO (p.58: 500-1,000 mg) after confirming no dose in the last 4 hours, no liver disease or hypersensitivity, and no overdose signs (nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain)
triggers: no Tylenol in the last four hours

expected.actionEn: Entonox, self-administered, only after the primary survey, pain assessment, baseline vitals with SpO2 and the chest exam; ventilation on, cylinder inverted 3 times (p.65)

Verbalize the Entonox decision: indicated for pain, no p.65 contraindication (pregnancy is not listed), shock is a caution to recheck with every set; omitting it only because she is pregnant is an error
triggers: shock is a caution for Entonox

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs, collar and straps, the pad and all interventions after every move and about every 5-6 minutes
Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes; interpret the trend (SBP 102 to 98, pulse 110 to 114): still above 90 so no bolus, but keep the Hypovolemia interventions and recheck
Reassess pain after the analgesics (abdomen and neck) and document the response

PCP: vascular access en route; verbalize the bolus trigger (SBP under 90: 20 mL/kg, maximum 2 L, reassess every 500 mL) and that TXA is not indicated unless shock secondary to blood loss develops (p.54, p.78)
En-route notification: pregnant trauma patient, 32 weeks, abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, contractions, spinal precautions, ETA
Complete hand-off: mechanism incl intrusion and restraint, obstetric history, findings, vitals trend, spinal restriction, oxygen
State the analgesic decisions with reasons: acetaminophen and Entonox given with times, ibuprofen withheld (pregnancy, p.68)
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes (mechanism, gestation, contraction interval, bleeding amount, vitals trend, analgesic times)

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate states or decides that her spine is clear, or that no c-spine control or spinal motion restriction is needed, for example because she climbed out of the car and walked to the curb, or because she is alert and says she feels fine. Saying that walking does NOT clear her spine, or that she needs c-spine control, is NOT this event.

candidate moves the patient or has her moved, lets or asks her to turn or move her head, or applies a pain stimulus (palpates the neck, presses on the abdomen) before manual stabilization of the head and neck has been started. Telling her to keep her head still is NOT this event.

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) releases manual stabilization of the head before she is fully secured to the spinal device with the collar, body straps and head blocks; applying the collar alone does not permit release. Handing manual stabilization over to the partner or to fire rescue (with instructions) is NOT a release.
candidate tapes the patient's head to the spinal device
candidate lets or asks the patient to stand up, walk, or walk to the ambulance or cot at any point in the call

candidate moves, rolls, lifts or repositions the patient repeatedly without need (for example more than one transfer onto a device, or extra rolls or lifts beyond one coordinated move onto the spinal device and one lift onto the cot)
candidate gives acetaminophen at a dose outside 500-1,000 mg (for example 1,500 mg or 2 g), by a route other than by mouth, or a second dose during this call
candidate gives Entonox without verbalizing inverting the cylinder 3 times before use

candidate gives Entonox although her chest has not been assessed up to that moment (no auscultation and no air-entry or chest-rise check of both sides, either in the primary survey or in the exam), or only asks her whether she has a collapsed lung instead of examining her chest. An air-entry or chest-rise check of both sides made earlier in the primary survey counts as assessed.

PCP starts or runs a fluid bolus (20 mL/kg or any fluid challenge) while SBP is at or above 90 and she is not hypoperfused. Vascular access with a saline lock or a keep-vein-open rate is NOT this event.

drugs.doseEn: inhalation, self-administered through the demand valve; indicated for her pain; invert the cylinder 3 times and turn the vehicle ventilation on first; only after the primary survey, pain assessment, baseline vitals with SpO2 and the history and exam needed to rule out contraindications; pregnancy is NOT a p.65 contraindication
drugs.contraindicationsEn: inability to comply; inability to ventilate an enclosed treatment area; decompression sickness; altered level of consciousness; pneumothorax; air embolism; inhalation injury; nitroglycerin in the last 5 minutes
drugs.cautionsEn: shock; abdominal distention; depressant drugs; COPD; facial injuries

drugs.doseEn: 1000 mg PO (guideline range 500-1000 mg PO; may repeat once after 4 hours); may be used with Entonox
drugs.contraindicationsEn: hypersensitivity; severe hepatic impairment or severe active liver disease; acetaminophen within the past 4 hours; suspected overdose (nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain)

drugs.doseEn: WITHHELD in this scenario: pregnancy (first, second or third trimester) is a listed contraindication (p.68). If a candidate actually gives it, record drug:ibuprofen.
drugs.contraindicationsEn: hypersensitivity to ibuprofen or other NSAIDs; active GI hemorrhage or ulcers; pregnancy (first, second or third trimester); anticoagulants

drugs.doseEn: NOT indicated in this scenario while there is no shock secondary to blood loss; if it were ever given: 2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute, within 3 hours of injury
drugs.contraindicationsEn: known hypersensitivity or allergy to TXA; more than 3 hours after injury; patient under 12 years; isolated TBI
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

drugs.doseEn: fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL, ONLY if SBP falls below 90 or she becomes hypoperfused; NOT indicated at SBP 102 or 98 - vascular access with a saline lock or keep-vein-open rate only

examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: You did a rapid body survey - what did you find on her neck, her abdomen and her pelvis?

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: manual stabilization, collar and spinal device, oxygen, a pad for the bleeding, supine and warm, one coordinated lift, oral acetaminophen 1,000 mg and Entonox (both within EMR scope); ibuprofen is withheld for pregnancy. No IV, no fluid, no TXA, no Functional Enquiry. Textbook practice (not a BC rubric item): tilting the whole spinal device to the left in the third trimester.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds vascular access en route, a 20 mL/kg bolus (maximum 2 L, reassess every 500 mL) only if SBP falls below 90 or she becomes hypoperfused, TXA (2 g IV push over 1 minute) only if shock secondary to blood loss develops within 3 hours of injury, and the 9-system Functional Enquiry. Analgesia is the same as for EMR: acetaminophen and Entonox, no ibuprofen.

sourcePages: Scenario tr-13 (data/practical/scenarios-2.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (mechanism: high risk automobile crash, intrusion >0.3 m on the occupant side or >0.5 m at any site); p.11 Primary Survey intervention indications (cervical spine stabilization, oxygen for trauma); p.12 critical history questions for an MVA; p.25 Spinal Management (manual stabilization, hard collar, spinal immobilization device, foam rollers or blocks, secure the body, do not tape the head); p.32 Abdominal Injuries (control external hemorrhage, limit patient movement, protect against heat loss, position of comfort, transport; PCP vascular access and TXA if indicated); p.50 Oxygen Administration (titrate to SpO2 94%); p.54 Hypovolemia (all-level interventions, PCP vascular access and fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L reassessing every 500 mL, note 2 anticipated shock); p.58 Acetaminophen (500-1,000 mg PO, contraindications); p.65 Entonox (contraindications, cautions, prerequisites, invert the cylinder 3 times); p.68 Ibuprofen (pregnancy in any trimester is a contraindication); p.78 Tranexamic Acid (2 g IV push over 1 minute, within 3 hours).
